sanskrit: yatra rājñā kubereṇa varā labdhāś ca puṣkalāḥ dhanādhipatyaṃ sakhyaṃ ca rudreṇāmitatejasā
english: There it was that King Kubera obtained abundant boons, and from Rudra of measureless splendour he won lordship over wealth and friendship besides.

sanskrit: suratvaṃ lokapālatvaṃ putraṃ ca nalakūbaram yatra lebhe mahābāho dhanādhipatir añjasā
english: There, O mighty-armed one, the lord of riches readily gained godhood, the office of world-guardian, and a son, Nalakūbara.

sanskrit: abhiṣiktaś ca tatraiva samāgamya marudgaṇaiḥ vāhanaṃ cāsya tad dattaṃ haṃsayuktaṃ manoramam vimānaṃ puṣpakaṃ divyaṃ nairṛtaiśvaryam eva ca
english: There too he was consecrated, having assembled with the hosts of the Maruts; and to him was given that lovely conveyance yoked with swans, the celestial Puṣpaka chariot, and the sovereignty over the Nairṛtas as well.

sanskrit: tatrāplutya balo rājan dattvā dāyāṃś ca puṣkalān jagāma tvarito rāmas tīrthaṃ śvetānulepanaḥ
english: Having bathed there, O king, and bestowed lavish gifts, Bala — Rāma, smeared with white unguents — went on in haste to the next holy ford.

sanskrit: niṣevitaṃ sarvasattvair nāmnā badarapācanam nānartukavanopetaṃ sadāpuṣpaphalaṃ śubham
english: It was frequented by all living beings, Badarapācana by name, graced with groves of every season, ever blossoming and fruitful and fair.

sanskrit: vaiśaṃpāyana uvāca tatas tīrthavaraṃ rāmo yayau badarapācanam tapasvisiddhacaritaṃ yatra kanyā dhṛtavratā
english: Vaiśaṃpāyana said: Then Rāma proceeded to the excellent ford named Badarapācana, hallowed by the deeds of ascetics and adepts, where a maiden, firm in her vows, once dwelt.

sanskrit: bharadvājasya duhitā rūpeṇāpratimā bhuvi srucāvatī nāma vibho kumārī brahmacāriṇī
english: She was the daughter of Bharadvāja, peerless in beauty upon the earth, O lord, a maiden named Srucāvatī, who lived in chastity.

sanskrit: tapaś cacāra sātyugraṃ niyamair bahubhir nṛpa bhartā me devarājaḥ syād iti niścitya bhāminī
english: She practised the fiercest austerity through many observances, O king, that lovely woman, having resolved within herself, 'May the king of the gods become my husband.'

sanskrit: samās tasyā vyatikrāntā bahvyaḥ kurukulodvaha carantyā niyamāṃs tāṃs tān strībhis tīvrān suduścarān
english: Many years passed over her, O upholder of the Kuru line, as she kept those several vows, severe and most hard for women to fulfil.

sanskrit: tasyās tu tena vṛttena tapasā ca viśāṃ pate bhaktyā ca bhagavān prītaḥ parayā pākaśāsanaḥ
english: By that conduct of hers, by her austerity, O lord of peoples, and by her supreme devotion, the divine Punisher of Pāka was well pleased.

sanskrit: ājagāmāśramaṃ tasyās tridaśādhipatiḥ prabhuḥ āsthāya rūpaṃ viprarṣer vasiṣṭhasya mahātmanaḥ
english: The lord and sovereign of the thirty gods came to her hermitage, having assumed the form of the brahmin sage, the great-souled Vasiṣṭha.

sanskrit: sā taṃ dṛṣṭvogratapasaṃ vasiṣṭhaṃ tapatāṃ varam ācārair munibhir dṛṣṭaiḥ pūjayām āsa bhārata
english: Seeing him of dread austerity, Vasiṣṭha, foremost among those who do penance, she honoured him with the rites prescribed by the sages, O Bhārata.

sanskrit: uvāca niyamajñā ca kalyāṇī sā priyaṃvadā bhagavan muniśārdūla kim ājñāpayasi prabho
english: And that auspicious maiden, versed in observances and sweet of speech, said: 'Reverend one, tiger among sages, what do you command, O lord?'

sanskrit: sarvam adya yathāśakti tava dāsyāmi suvrata śakrabhaktyā tu te pāṇiṃ na dāsyāmi kathaṃ cana
english: 'All that lies in my power I will give you this day, O firm in vows; yet out of my devotion to Śakra I will in no wise give you my hand.'

sanskrit: vrataiś ca niyamaiś caiva tapasā ca tapodhana śakras toṣayitavyo vai mayā tribhuvaneśvaraḥ
english: 'By vows and observances and by austerity, O wealth of penance, it is Śakra, lord of the three worlds, whom I must satisfy.'

sanskrit: ity ukto bhagavān devaḥ smayann iva nirīkṣya tām uvāca niyamajñāṃ tāṃ sāntvayann iva bhārata
english: Thus addressed, the divine lord, gazing upon her as though with a smile, spoke to her who knew the observances, soothing her as it were, O Bhārata.

sanskrit: ugraṃ tapaś carasi vai viditā me 'si suvrate yadartham ayam ārambhas tava kalyāṇi hṛdgataḥ
english: 'Fierce is the austerity you practise; well do I know you, O firm in vows. The purpose for which this endeavour lies in your heart, O auspicious one —'

sanskrit: tac ca sarvaṃ yathābhūtaṃ bhaviṣyati varānane tapasā labhyate sarvaṃ sarvaṃ tapasi tiṣṭhati
english: '— all that shall come to pass even as it is, O fair-faced one. By austerity all things are won; all things rest upon austerity.'

sanskrit: yāni sthānāni divyāni vibudhānāṃ śubhānane tapasā tāni prāpyāni tapomūlaṃ mahat sukham
english: 'Those celestial realms that belong to the gods, O fair of face, are to be attained by austerity; great bliss is rooted in austerity.'

sanskrit: iha kṛtvā tapo ghoraṃ dehaṃ saṃnyasya mānavāḥ devatvaṃ yānti kalyāṇi śṛṇu cedaṃ vaco mama
english: 'Having performed dread austerity here and laid aside the body, mortals attain godhood, O auspicious one. Now hear this word of mine.'

sanskrit: pacasvaitāni subhage badarāṇi śubhavrate pacety uktvā sa bhagavāñ jagāma balasūdanaḥ
english: 'Cook these jujubes, O fortunate one, O fair in vows — cook them,' said that divine slayer of Bala, and departed.

sanskrit: āmantrya tāṃ tu kalyāṇīṃ tato japyaṃ jajāpa saḥ avidūre tatas tasmād āśramāt tīrtha uttame indratīrthe mahārāja triṣu lokeṣu viśrute
english: Having taken leave of that auspicious maiden, he then murmured his sacred recitation not far from that hermitage, at the excellent ford, the Indratīrtha, O great king, renowned throughout the three worlds.

sanskrit: tasyā jijñāsanārthaṃ sa bhagavān pākaśāsanaḥ badarāṇām apacanaṃ cakāra vibudhādhipaḥ
english: To put her to the test, the divine Punisher of Pāka, lord of the gods, caused the jujubes not to cook.

sanskrit: tataḥ sa prayatā rājan vāgyatā vigataklamā tatparā śucisaṃvītā pāvake samadhiśrayat apacad rājaśārdūla badarāṇi mahāvratā
english: Then, O king, with self restrained, speech curbed, and weariness gone, intent upon her task and clad in spotless raiment, she set them on the fire; she of mighty vows cooked the jujubes, O tiger among kings.

sanskrit: tasyāḥ pacantyāḥ sumahān kālo 'gāt puruṣarṣabha na ca sma tāny apacyanta dinaṃ ca kṣayam abhyagāt
english: As she cooked, a very long while passed, O bull among men, yet the fruits would not soften, and the day drew toward its close.

sanskrit: hutāśanena dagdhaś ca yas tasyāḥ kāṣṭhasaṃcayaḥ akāṣṭham agniṃ sā dṛṣṭvā svaśarīram athādahat
english: When the fire had consumed her store of firewood, seeing the flame bereft of fuel, she then set her own body to burn.

sanskrit: pādau prakṣipya sā pūrvaṃ pāvake cārudarśanā dagdhau dagdhau punaḥ pādāv upāvartayatānaghā
english: Casting first her two feet into the flame, that fair maiden, the blameless one, turned her feet back ever again into it as they burned and burned.

sanskrit: caraṇau dahyamānau ca nācintayad aninditā duḥkhaṃ kamalapatrākṣī maharṣeḥ priyakāmyayā
english: Though her feet were being consumed, the irreproachable one, lotus-petal-eyed, gave no thought to her pain, longing only to please the great sage.

sanskrit: atha tat karma dṛṣṭvāsyāḥ prītas tribhuvaneśvaraḥ tataḥ saṃdarśayām āsa kanyāyai rūpam ātmanaḥ
english: Then, beholding this deed of hers, the lord of the three worlds was well pleased, and thereupon revealed to the maiden his own true form.

sanskrit: uvāca ca suraśreṣṭhas tāṃ kanyāṃ sudṛḍhavratām prīto 'smi te śubhe bhaktyā tapasā niyamena ca
english: And the foremost of the gods said to that maiden of unbending vows: 'I am pleased with you, O fair one, by your devotion, your austerity, and your observance.'

sanskrit: tasmād yo 'bhimataḥ kāmaḥ sa te saṃpatsyate śubhe dehaṃ tyaktvā mahābhāge tridive mayi vatsyasi
english: 'Therefore whatever desire is dear to you shall be fulfilled, O fair one; and laying aside your body, O greatly blessed, you shall dwell with me in heaven.'

sanskrit: idaṃ ca te tīrthavaraṃ sthiraṃ loke bhaviṣyati sarvapāpāpahaṃ subhru nāmnā badarapācanam vikhyātaṃ triṣu lokeṣu brahmarṣibhir abhiplutam
english: 'And this excellent ford of yours shall stand abiding in the world, washing away all sins, O fair-browed one — Badarapācana by name, renowned throughout the three worlds, frequented by brahmin sages.'

sanskrit: asmin khalu mahābhāge śubhe tīrthavare purā tyaktvā saptarṣayo jagmur himavantam arundhatīm
english: 'For at this excellent and auspicious ford, O greatly blessed one, the Seven Sages of old once departed and went to the Himālaya, leaving Arundhatī behind.'

sanskrit: tatas te vai mahābhāgā gatvā tatra susaṃśitāḥ vṛttyarthaṃ phalamūlāni samāhartuṃ yayuḥ kila
english: 'Then those greatly blessed and well-disciplined sages, having gone thither, set forth, it is said, to gather fruits and roots for their sustenance.'

sanskrit: teṣāṃ vṛttyarthināṃ tatra vasatāṃ himavadvane anāvṛṣṭir anuprāptā tadā dvādaśavārṣikī
english: 'As they dwelt there seeking their livelihood in the Himālayan forest, a drought set in then that lasted twelve years.'

sanskrit: te kṛtvā cāśramaṃ tatra nyavasanta tapasvinaḥ arundhaty api kalyāṇī taponityābhavat tadā
english: 'Those ascetics, having made a hermitage there, took up their abode; and the auspicious Arundhatī too was at that time ever steadfast in austerity.'

sanskrit: arundhatīṃ tato dṛṣṭvā tīvraṃ niyamam āsthitām athāgamat trinayanaḥ suprīto varadas tadā
english: 'Then beholding Arundhatī engaged in fierce observance, the three-eyed god, bestower of boons, came to her, greatly pleased.'

sanskrit: brāhmaṃ rūpaṃ tataḥ kṛtvā mahādevo mahāyaśāḥ tām abhyetyābravīd devo bhikṣām icchāmy ahaṃ śubhe
english: 'Then Mahādeva of great renown, having assumed the form of a brahmin, approached her and said: "I wish for alms, O fair one."'

sanskrit: pratyuvāca tataḥ sā taṃ brāhmaṇaṃ cārudarśanā kṣīṇo 'nnasaṃcayo vipra badarāṇīha bhakṣaya tato 'bravīn mahādevaḥ pacasvaitāni suvrate
english: 'Then that fair maiden answered the brahmin: "Our store of food is spent, O brahmin; eat these jujubes here." Thereupon Mahādeva said: "Cook these, O firm in vows."'

sanskrit: ity uktā sāpacat tāni brāhmaṇapriyakāmyayā adhiśritya samiddhe 'gnau badarāṇi yaśasvinī
english: 'Thus addressed, that illustrious woman, wishing to please the brahmin, set the jujubes upon the kindled fire and cooked them.'

sanskrit: divyā manoramāḥ puṇyāḥ kathāḥ śuśrāva sā tadā atītā sā tv anāvṛṣṭir ghorā dvādaśavārṣikī
english: 'Meanwhile she listened to divine, delightful, and holy tales; and so passed away that dreadful drought of twelve years.'

sanskrit: anaśnantyāḥ pacantyāś ca śṛṇvantyāś ca kathāḥ śubhāḥ ahaḥsamaḥ sa tasyās tu kālo 'tītaḥ sudāruṇaḥ
english: 'As she fasted and cooked and hearkened to those auspicious tales, that most grievous span of time passed for her as though it were a single day.'

sanskrit: tatas te munayaḥ prāptāḥ phalāny ādāya parvatāt tataḥ sa bhagavān prītaḥ provācārundhatīṃ tadā
english: 'Then those sages arrived, bringing fruits from the mountain; and thereupon the pleased lord spoke to Arundhatī.'

sanskrit: upasarpasva dharmajñe yathāpūrvam imān ṛṣīn prīto 'smi tava dharmajñe tapasā niyamena ca
english: '"Draw near, O knower of duty, to these sages as before. I am pleased with you, O knower of duty, by your austerity and your observance."'

sanskrit: tataḥ saṃdarśayām āsa svarūpaṃ bhagavān haraḥ tato 'bravīt tadā tebhyas tasyās tac caritaṃ mahat
english: 'Then the lord Hara revealed his own true form, and thereupon recounted to them that great deed of hers.'

sanskrit: bhavadbhir himavatpṛṣṭhe yat tapaḥ samupārjitam asyāś ca yat tapo viprā na samaṃ tan mataṃ mama
english: '"The austerity that you gained upon the slopes of the Himālaya, O brahmins, and the austerity of this woman — these I deem not equal."'

sanskrit: anayā hi tapasvinyā tapas taptaṃ suduścaram anaśnantyā pacantyā ca samā dvādaśa pāritāḥ
english: '"For by this ascetic woman austerity most hard to perform was practised; fasting and cooking, she has carried through twelve full years."'

sanskrit: tataḥ provāca bhagavāṃs tām evārundhatīṃ punaḥ varaṃ vṛṇīṣva kalyāṇi yat te 'bhilaṣitaṃ hṛdi
english: 'Then the lord again spoke to that same Arundhatī: "Choose a boon, O auspicious one, whatever you desire in your heart."'

sanskrit: sābravīt pṛthutāmrākṣī devaṃ saptarṣisaṃsadi bhagavān yadi me prītas tīrthaṃ syād idam uttamam siddhadevarṣidayitaṃ nāmnā badarapācanam
english: 'She of wide coppery eyes said to the god in the assembly of the Seven Sages: "If, O lord, you are pleased with me, may this become an excellent ford, dear to the Siddhas, gods, and sages, Badarapācana by name."'

sanskrit: tathāsmin devadeveśa trirātram uṣitaḥ śuciḥ prāpnuyād upavāsena phalaṃ dvādaśavārṣikam evam astv iti tāṃ coktvā haro yātas tadā divam
english: '"And, O lord of the lords of gods, may one who dwells here in purity for three nights gain by his fasting the fruit of twelve years." Saying to her, "So be it," Hara then departed to heaven.'

sanskrit: ṛṣayo vismayaṃ jagmus tāṃ dṛṣṭvā cāpy arundhatīm aśrāntāṃ cāvivarṇāṃ ca kṣutpipāsāsahāṃ satīm
english: 'The sages were filled with wonder, beholding Arundhatī unwearied and unfaded, the chaste one who had borne hunger and thirst.'

sanskrit: evaṃ siddhiḥ parā prāptā arundhatyā viśuddhayā yathā tvayā mahābhāge madarthaṃ saṃśitavrate
english: 'Thus did the pure Arundhatī attain supreme perfection — even as you, O greatly blessed one of unbending vows, have done for my sake.'

sanskrit: viśeṣo hi tvayā bhadre vrate hy asmin samarpitaḥ tathā cedaṃ dadāmy adya niyamena sutoṣitaḥ
english: 'For a still greater devotion, O gentle one, have you given to this vow; and so this day, well pleased by your observance, I grant you this.'

sanskrit: viśeṣaṃ tava kalyāṇi prayacchāmi varaṃ vare arundhatyā varas tasyā yo datto vai mahātmanā
english: 'A special boon I grant you, O auspicious and excellent one, beyond that boon which the great-souled god bestowed upon Arundhatī.'

sanskrit: tasya cāhaṃ prasādena tava kalyāṇi tejasā pravakṣyāmy aparaṃ bhūyo varam atra yathāvidhi
english: 'And by his grace and by your own splendour, O auspicious one, I shall now declare here yet another boon in due form.'

sanskrit: yas tv ekāṃ rajanīṃ tīrthe vatsyate susamāhitaḥ sa snātvā prāpsyate lokān dehanyāsāc ca durlabhān
english: 'Whoever shall dwell at this ford for a single night with mind well composed, having bathed, shall upon the laying aside of his body attain worlds hard to win.'

sanskrit: ity uktvā bhagavān devaḥ sahasrākṣaḥ pratāpavān srucāvatīṃ tataḥ puṇyāṃ jagāma tridivaṃ punaḥ
english: Having so spoken to the holy Srucāvatī, the mighty thousand-eyed god then returned again to heaven.

sanskrit: gate vajradhare rājaṃs tatra varṣaṃ papāta ha puṣpāṇāṃ bharataśreṣṭha divyānāṃ divyagandhinām
english: When the wielder of the thunderbolt had gone, O king, a rain of celestial flowers fell there, sweet with celestial fragrance, O best of the Bharatas.

sanskrit: nedur dundubhayaś cāpi samantāt sumahāsvanāḥ mārutaś ca vavau yuktyā puṇyagandho viśāṃ pate
english: Kettledrums of mighty sound resounded on every side, and a fragrant, gentle breeze blew fittingly, O lord of peoples.

sanskrit: utsṛjya tu śubhaṃ dehaṃ jagāmendrasya bhāryatām tapasogreṇa sā labdhvā tena reme sahācyuta
english: And casting off her fair body, she passed to the state of Indra's consort, having won it by fierce austerity, and rejoiced together with that imperishable lord.

sanskrit: janamejaya uvāca kā tasyā bhagavan mātā kva saṃvṛddhā ca śobhanā śrotum icchāmy ahaṃ brahman paraṃ kautūhalaṃ hi me
english: Janamejaya said: Who, O reverend one, was her mother, and where was that lovely maiden reared? I wish to hear, O brahmin, for great is my curiosity.

sanskrit: vaiśaṃpāyana uvāca bhāradvājasya viprarṣeḥ skannaṃ reto mahātmanaḥ dṛṣṭvāpsarasam āyāntīṃ ghṛtācīṃ pṛthulocanām
english: Vaiśaṃpāyana said: When the great-souled brahmin sage Bhāradvāja beheld the wide-eyed apsaras Ghṛtācī approaching, his seed was shed.

sanskrit: sa tu jagrāha tad retaḥ kareṇa japatāṃ varaḥ tadāvapat parṇapuṭe tatra sā saṃbhavac chubhā
english: That foremost of those who murmur prayers caught the seed in his hand and cast it into a cup of leaves; and therein that fair maiden came into being.

sanskrit: tasyās tu jātakarmādi kṛtvā sarvaṃ tapodhanaḥ nāma cāsyāḥ sa kṛtavān bhāradvājo mahāmuniḥ
english: Having performed for her all the birth-rites and the rest, the great sage Bhāradvāja, that wealth of penance, bestowed upon her a name.

sanskrit: srucāvatīti dharmātmā tadarṣigaṇasaṃsadi sa ca tām āśrame nyasya jagāma himavadvanam
english: 'Srucāvatī' — so the righteous one named her in the assembly of the sages; and leaving her in the hermitage, he went to the Himālayan forest.

sanskrit: tatrāpy upaspṛśya mahānubhāvo; vasūni dattvā ca mahādvijebhyaḥ jagāma tīrthaṃ susamāhitātmā; śakrasya vṛṣṇipravaras tadānīm
english: There too the high-souled foremost of the Vṛṣṇis, having touched the waters and given wealth to the great brahmins, went with well-composed soul to the ford of Śakra at that time.

sanskrit: vaiśaṃpāyana uvāca indratīrthaṃ tato gatvā yadūnāṃ pravaro balī viprebhyo dhanaratnāni dadau snātvā yathāvidhi
english: Vaiśaṃpāyana said: Having then gone to the Indratīrtha, the mighty foremost of the Yadus, after bathing in due form, gave wealth and jewels to the brahmins.

sanskrit: tatra hy amararājo 'sāv īje kratuśatena ha bṛhaspateś ca deveśaḥ pradadau vipulaṃ dhanam
english: For there that king of the immortals worshipped with a hundred sacrifices, and the lord of the gods bestowed abundant wealth upon Bṛhaspati.

sanskrit: nirargalān sajārūthyān sarvān vividhadakṣiṇān ājahāra kratūṃs tatra yathoktān vedapāragaiḥ
english: Unhindered rites, attended by the jārūthya offerings, all with manifold sacrificial fees, he performed there as prescribed, with priests deeply versed in the Vedas.

sanskrit: tān kratūn bharataśreṣṭha śatakṛtvo mahādyutiḥ pūrayām āsa vidhivat tataḥ khyātaḥ śatakratuḥ
english: Those sacrifices, O best of the Bharatas, the one of great splendour duly accomplished a hundred times over, and thence became renowned as Śatakratu, 'lord of a hundred rites.'

sanskrit: tasya nāmnā ca tat tīrthaṃ śivaṃ puṇyaṃ sanātanam indratīrtham iti khyātaṃ sarvapāpapramocanam
english: And by his name that ford, blessed, holy, and eternal, became famed as the Indratīrtha, the deliverer from all sins.

sanskrit: upaspṛśya ca tatrāpi vidhivan musalāyudhaḥ brāhmaṇān pūjayitvā ca pānācchādanabhojanaiḥ śubhaṃ tīrthavaraṃ tasmād rāmatīrthaṃ jagāma ha
english: Having there too touched the waters in due form, the wielder of the pestle honoured the brahmins with drink, raiment, and food, and from that excellent and auspicious ford went on to Rāmatīrtha.

sanskrit: yatra rāmo mahābhāgo bhārgavaḥ sumahātapāḥ asakṛt pṛthivīṃ sarvāṃ hatakṣatriyapuṃgavām
english: There the greatly blessed Rāma, scion of Bhṛgu, of mighty austerity, again and again rid the whole earth of its foremost warriors of the Kṣatriya race.

sanskrit: upādhyāyaṃ puraskṛtya kaśyapaṃ munisattamam ayajad vājapeyena so 'śvamedhaśatena ca pradadau dakṣiṇārthaṃ ca pṛthivīṃ vai sasāgarām
english: Setting at the fore his preceptor Kaśyapa, best of sages, he worshipped with the Vājapeya rite and with a hundred horse-sacrifices, and gave away as the sacrificial fee the whole earth with its seas.

sanskrit: rāmo dattvā dhanaṃ tatra dvijebhyo janamejaya upaspṛśya yathānyāyaṃ pūjayitvā tathā dvijān
english: Rāma, having given wealth there to the brahmins, O Janamejaya, touched the waters according to rule and likewise honoured the twice-born,

sanskrit: puṇye tīrthe śubhe deśe vasu dattvā śubhānanaḥ munīṃś caivābhivādyātha yamunātīrtham āgamat
english: and at that holy ford, in that auspicious place, the fair-faced one bestowed wealth and saluted the sages, and then came to the Yamunātīrtha.

sanskrit: yatrānayām āsa tadā rājasūyaṃ mahīpate putro 'diter mahābhāgo varuṇo vai sitaprabhaḥ
english: There it was that the greatly blessed son of Aditi, Varuṇa of white radiance, once conducted the Rājasūya sacrifice, O lord of the earth.

sanskrit: tatra nirjitya saṃgrāme mānuṣān daivatāṃs tathā varaṃ kratuṃ samājahre varuṇaḥ paravīrahā
english: There, having vanquished in battle both men and gods, Varuṇa, slayer of hostile heroes, performed that excellent sacrifice.

sanskrit: tasmin kratuvare vṛtte saṃgrāmaḥ samajāyata devānāṃ dānavānāṃ ca trailokyasya kṣayāvahaḥ
english: When that excellent sacrifice was concluded, a war arose between the gods and the dānavas, bringing destruction upon the three worlds.

sanskrit: rājasūye kratuśreṣṭhe nivṛtte janamejaya jāyate sumahāghoraḥ saṃgrāmaḥ kṣatriyān prati
english: When the Rājasūya, that foremost of sacrifices, is brought to its close, O Janamejaya, a most terrible war arises that falls upon the Kṣatriyas.
